purpose: Classifies a malleolar (ankle) fracture by the level of the fibular injury relative to the syndesmosis, within the AO/OTA compendium used to standardise fracture communication and recording.
issuer: AO Foundation and Orthopaedic Trauma Association
system: AO/OTA Fracture and Dislocation Classification Compendium 2018: malleolar segment 44 (types A, B, C by the level of the fibular injury relative to the syndesmosis)

summary.text: This card is the AO/OTA 2018 classification (malleolar segment 44). The compendium does not state a correspondence to the Danis-Weber classification; the Weber names are search aliases only.

locator.section: Malleolar segment 44, pp S65-S69 (the source does not mention Weber or Danis-Weber)

summary.text: The AO/OTA 2018 malleolar segment (44) classifies an ankle fracture into type A, B or C by the level of the fibular injury relative to the syndesmosis: infrasyndesmotic, transsyndesmotic or suprasyndesmotic.
Each type divides into three groups and each group into three subgroups, by the medial and posterior injury and by the fibular fracture pattern; qualifications are optional lower-case suffixes.

locator.section: Malleolar segment, Groups, Subgroups and Qualifications note

summary.text: The malleolar pages give morphology and codes only; they state no management or prognosis for any type.

The card lists classification codes, not what plain film can show: several subgroups are ligament ruptures and the syndesmosis qualifiers are not imaging methods, and the source gives no imaging method.

definitions.text: 44A, infrasyndesmotic fibula injury: a rupture of the lateral collateral ligament, an avulsion of the lateral malleolar tip or a transverse lateral malleolar fracture, alone or with a medial or posteromedial injury.
44B, transsyndesmotic fibula fracture: isolated (44B1), with a medial injury (44B2), or with a medial injury and a fracture of the posterolateral rim, Volkmann's fragment (44B3).
44C, suprasyndesmotic fibula injury: a simple or wedge or multifragmentary diaphyseal fibula fracture (44C1, 44C2) or a proximal fibula injury (44C3).
Qualifications are optional descriptive terms, written as a lower-case letter in brackets in place of the asterisk of a code; more than one can be applied, separated by a comma.

pitfalls.text: An isolated medial malleolar fracture is not a 44: it is coded as a tibial distal end segment partial articular fracture (43B1.2 or 43B2.2). With a lateral-side ankle injury it is a 44.
A fracture of the posterior articular margin (Volkmann) without a lesion of the fibula is a distal tibial end segment fracture (43B1.1 or 43B2.1), not a 44.
A fibula fracture that is part of an ankle fracture is coded 44. The separate fibula code (4F) is for fibular fractures not associated with an ankle fracture.
